sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Project commands and libraries
sections.what: Lists the project's name and version, the commands to run it, the libraries the site needs, and the tools used only during development. The build command also runs an extra script after the Next.js build.
sections.why: Standard way for a Node project to declare commands and libraries.
sections.watch_out: The build command runs scripts/home.mjs after the build. If that file is missing or fails, the build fails.

summary: Declares the project's name, the commands used to run and build it, the libraries it needs, and the tools used only during development.
purpose: Tells npm and developers how to start, build and lint the site, and which versions of its libraries to install.
why: This is the standard place for a Node project to declare its commands and libraries.
how: Lists four commands: dev starts a development server, build runs the Next.js build and then an extra script, start serves the built site, lint checks the code. Then it lists the runtime libraries and the development tools.
inputs: Read by npm when installing packages or running a command.
outputs: Installed packages and the results of each command.
risks: The build command runs scripts/home.mjs after the build. That file is not in this packet, so a missing or failing script breaks the build. There is no test command.
debug: If install fails, check the version ranges. If build fails after Next.js finishes, look at scripts/home.mjs. If lint reports problems, run it directly to see the messages.
